questions.stem: What is the key difference between a strong acid and a weak acid?

options.text: Strong acids completely ionise in water; weak acids only partially ionise
Strong acids have a higher boiling point

questions.explanation: A strong acid completely ionises (100%) in water, shown by a single arrow (→). A weak acid only partially ionises (typically less than 5%), shown by equilibrium arrows (⇌). This is different from concentrated/dilute, which describes the amount of acid present.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a weak acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid (found in vinegar) is a weak acid because it only partially ionises in water. The three common strong acids are hydrochloric acid (HCl), sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), and nitric acid (HNO₃), which all completely ionise.
